profiles.name: Mate Rimac
profiles.title: Mate Rimac: from an electric BMW to the Concept_One
profiles.description: How Mate Rimac's electric BMW project led to the Concept_One: four motors, torque control and the engineering behind the founder's story.
profiles.intro: Mate Rimac is the founder of Rimac Automobili. His company's account traces the project to a 1984 BMW E30 whose combustion engine failed during a race. He replaced the powertrain with an electric one. The interesting question is what happened between that conversion and a car designed around electricity from the start.
sections: A conversion is a starting point

Rimac's company history describes the electric BMW as the beginning of a much broader engineering effort. It identifies powertrain, battery and control-system development as work carried out inside the business. That helps explain why the founder's story belongs in a car-design collection: the shape of a finished car depends on the systems its team can build and integrate.

Rimac presented the production Concept_One at the 2016 Geneva Motor Show. Its launch document describes four electric motors, one assigned to each wheel, with a control system that adjusts their torque separately. It also describes a dedicated vehicle platform, liquid battery thermal management and regenerative braking. These are claims about a particular production design, rather than specifications for every subsequent Rimac model.
Read the engineering behind the headline

Four motors make the control strategy as interesting as the combined power figure. In the Concept_One account, propulsion and braking are coordinated through individual wheel control. Our reading is that this changes the design question: how does the whole car manage the driver's request, rather than simply how large an engine can fit? Compare that question with the F40's turbocharged road-car brief and the Miura's transverse engine layout. Each is a different way to organise a dramatic sports car.
Questions to take to the sources

When reading a hypercar launch, separate the architecture from a performance promise. Which version is being described? Is an acceleration figure a manufacturer claim or an independently observed test? How are battery temperature and repeated use treated? The linked Concept_One release is a useful period document for asking those questions. It does not answer them for an individual used car, and this profile adds no road-test or ownership findings.
